guidelines.detail: refines ACT-03 (The description says the inspection begins after the identifying data is entered and that values are then collected automatically from the device. The generated model lacks the automatic connection step after data entry (M8) and merges the data entry into one task (M2). The reference models the connection as a serviceTask, which fits BPMN 2.0.2 because it is automated work. The guideline is kept g)

same as LRN-112 (P2 shows the generated gateway label restates the dependent step ('Depending on results, additional questions?') where the reference asks a yes/no question about the checked value. P1 shows a status-style label ('Inspection questions complete') on a gateway. M4 shows the reference has a check activity before the decision that the generated model lacks, so the gateway had no established condition t)

same as LRN-020 (The reference splits the machine type and the serial number into separate user tasks before the inspection begins, while the generated model combines them into one task. The description joins the two items with 'and' in a clause that gates the later inspection, which is the situation LRN-020 covers. The records show a real structural difference, so I propose the guideline with the same_as_learned )

refines FID-02 (The description says the user enters the machine type and the serial number before the inspection can begin. The generated model merged both into one user task, so the reference's separate 'Enter type of Machine' task has no counterpart (M2), and the reference's 'Enter serial number of machine' label matches the merged task (P4). The other differences are either label-wording variants (P1-P3) or r)

same as LRN-117 (Missing element M7 is a serviceTask that connects to the machine after the serial number entry, which the description implies (S2: after entering the machine type and serial number the inspection can begin; S3: values are automatically collected from the machine). The previous guideline already covers this, and the generator did not apply it, so the proposed rule restates LRN-117 in general terms.)

refines FID-02 (The generated model merged the automatic collection and the presentation into one serviceTask (P3 matched a single task to the reference collection task, while the reference has separate 'Show data' and 'Present results' serviceTasks, M9 and M10). The same clause also lists the button presses, which the generator modeled as one extra userTask (X3) instead of separate userTasks. The description joi)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that, after the user enters identifying data for a device, the application automatically connects to or collects data from that device, and later steps depend on that connection: Model the automatic connection as its own bpmn:serviceTask placed in sequence directly after the user task that captures the identifying data, and before any user task that depends on the connection. Do not fold the automatic connection into the data entry user task, and do not represent it as a user task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that, after the user enters identifying data for a device, the application automatically connects to or collects data from that device, and later steps depend on that connection

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a yes/no decision whose two outcomes are described as success or failure of a result, or as availability or non-availability of an option, and the branches lead to different next steps: Model the decision as an exclusive gateway and label it as a closed yes/no question that names the condition being tested, using the description's own terms for that condition (for example, whether the result works or whether the option can be obtained). Keep the same condition wording on the outgoing flows, and avoid generic labels such as 'Decision' or 'Check'.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that some further steps are performed or skipped depending on the outcome of an earlier check, and does not name the condition that is tested

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states one user action whose clause joins several distinct inputs or choices with 'and' (for example, 'provides X and Y' or 'selects A, B, and C'), followed by a further step that depends on them: Model each distinct input or choice named in that clause as its own user task, in the order the description states them, and connect these tasks in sequence before the task for the dependent step. Do not merge the items into one task, and do not leave any stated item out of the model.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states, in one introductory clause, that the user enters two separate identifying items (for example a type and an identifier number) before a later stage of the work can begin

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the user enters two or more distinct data items one after another before a later stage of the process begins: Model each separately described data entry as its own user task, in the order the description gives, and keep the later stage after the last entry. Do not combine the entries into one task, even when they are described together in one sentence.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the user enters two or more distinct data items one after another before a later stage of the process begins

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the application automatically collects data from a device and that the collected data is then presented to the user, whether both actions appear in one clause (for example, joined by 'and') or in separate clauses: Model the automatic collection as its own bpmn:serviceTask. Model the presentation of the collected data as a second, separate bpmn:serviceTask placed directly after the collection, in the order the description gives. Do not combine the collection and the presentation into one bpmn:serviceTask, even when one clause describes both. If the description states that the user presses a control before the collection starts, model each press as its own bpmn:userTask placed before the collection serviceTask.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the application automatically collects data from a device and that the collected data is then presented to the user, whether both actions appear in one clause (for example, joined by 'and') or in separate clauses
